sampling_model.design: The data are dominated and i.i.d. on the canonical full ball \(\mathcal V_P=\{P':\|dP'/dP-1\|_\infty<\varepsilon\}\), intersected with the full transported fixed-nullity, fixed-cokernel, reduced-modulus-separated stratum and both bridge-solvability loci. Every DQM curve remaining in that intersection is admissible; tangent richness is not part of the model definition.
sampling_model.units: The sampling units are \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,Z_i,W_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), independently distributed according to \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment \(A\) is binary. The statistical target is the observed joint-bridge functional; its equality with the ATE uses the separately stated latent consistency, exchangeability, positivity, negative-control, and bridge-compatibility conditions.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-bridge existence is an observed solvability restriction. The main model imposes no injectivity, surjectivity, preferred minimum-norm bridge, or bridge uniqueness.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The fold-indexed penalized-minimax or Galerkin ridge affine ensemble is an explicit candidate estimator. Its ridge uniqueness, affine centering, four-corner conversion, and mixed-bias algebra are valid. The current assumptions do not prove its learned projection rate because multiplier, dimension, training-dependence, coefficient-envelope, and population Gram null-space controls are incomplete.

Quotient-functional efficiency is prior art; the unresolved novelty is the coupled proximal tangent-lifting theorem, while the nested attaining projection is proved conditionally on that geometry and explicit estimator rates.

body.tldr: The observed-law model uses the full local \(L^\infty\) likelihood-ratio ball, the full fixed-defect spectrally separated operator stratum, and every DQM curve that remains in both bridge-solvability loci. Reverse score lifting on this unrestricted joint germ remains unresolved: continuous kernel projections do not supply a local parameterization of the coupled solvability intersection. The affine normal identity and all three positive finite tangent tests remain valid, including the exact \(36\)-cell efficiency value \(773723312/334026875\) and strict single-pair nonattainment. The general quotient projection is proved only conditional on both reverse lifting and bridge-score pathwise validity. The displayed learned-projection and Wald claims remain open because the primitive list lacks dimension-aware multiplier, same-training-sample concentration, Gram-null-space, and contiguous-path uniformity controls. The observed bridge functional equals a causal ATE only under the separate latent identification proposition.

project_justification.gap: Existing nonunique-bridge results provide regular inference under additional selection and regularity conditions, but they do not establish the full tangent closure of the simultaneous outcome- and treatment-solvability germ considered here. The present assumptions likewise do not yet turn continuous moving kernels into actual path lifts or certify the growing learned affine projection.
project_justification.niche: The proposed contribution is quotient-tangent efficiency for a saturated fixed-defect observed-law model in which both bridge fibers may be non-singleton. Its distinctive mathematical burden is the coupled score-lifting theorem, including the arms' shared \((W,X)\) marginal, together with an implementable estimator that learns the variance-minimizing affine score.
project_justification.fill: The established contribution currently consists of the affine normal identity, operator-kernel stability, exact finite tangent and nonattainment witnesses, the corrected outcome-only selected-parameter comparison, and conditional Hilbert and cross-fit reductions. General score lifting and primitive-to-Wald inference remain the two load-bearing open steps.

body.related_work: Bennett et al. provide penalized bridge inference under additional regularity, while Zhang et al. emphasize nonuniqueness; neither result is identified here with the unresolved global affine-quotient bound. Imbens et al. and Ai--Shan concern uniqueness-restricted or finite-dimensional efficiency regimes and therefore do not establish the two-fiber quotient tangent calculation. Severini--Tripathi is prior art for efficiency of quotient-like functionals, so the new burden is the simultaneous proximal incidence geometry rather than Hilbert projection alone. Ai--Chen and the proximal nuisance-rate literature motivate Galerkin and cross-fit calculations but do not supply the missing same-training-sample and null-space stability bounds for the displayed estimator. The final Bennett publisher theorem text has not been verified here, and no mathematical claim depends on an asserted difference from inaccessible text.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The central unresolved mathematical step is reverse score lifting on the unrestricted saturated infinite-dimensional intersection. Operator-norm continuity gives only continuous kernel projections, not differentiable bridge or kernel selections, a constant-rank chart for the coupled solvability loci, or the product control needed for every unbounded-support path derivative. The learned dictionary claim separately lacks fourth-moment multiplier envelopes, dimension-correct vector aggregation, valid concentration for dictionaries evaluated on their fitting sample, control of empirical ridge leakage through population Gram null directions, and locally uniform contiguous-path rates. Closed range also excludes generic compact infinite-rank inverse problems. Rank-changing unions, general direct-integral measurable charts, and a SUPPORT reanalysis remain outside the proved scope.
body.honest_scope: Unconditional results are the normal--affine algebra, operator perturbation, the positive finite regular witness, the singular branch witness, the transverse four-level witness, strict single-pair nonattainment, and the explicit outcome-only selected-parameter comparison. The general quotient formula is only a conditional Hilbert conclusion under reverse lifting and bridge-score pathwise validity. The general primitive learned-projection, regularity, efficiency-attainment, variance-ratio, and Wald theorems remain open. The observed bridge functional receives a causal ATE interpretation only from the separate latent identification proposition. No efficiency claim is made for arbitrary path-poor subcharts, rank-changing unions, generic compact ill-posed operators, or an external outcome-only model whose neighboring-law parameter has not been imported.
body.interpretation: With redundant proxies, a chosen bridge pair can define a valid score without minimizing variance over the affine score hull. The exact finite witness proves this phenomenon and supplies a computable variance-minimizing replacement on that germ. For the SUPPORT application, the result is presently a diagnostic and finite-projection prescription: it does not assert that the published proxy specification has nonunique bridges, and the general global-efficiency and Wald guarantees remain conditional on the unresolved lifting and learning steps.
